text:
maria: anyone else seeing odd scheduling in eu-west1 this morning? two canary pods failed to schedule with "FailedScheduling: 0/15 nodes are available: 15 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" even though `kubectl describe node` shows 1-2 free GPUs on several nodes
ryan: yeah noticed that too, looks like fragmentation — lots of nodes with 1 free GPU but pods request 2 GPUs so they sit pending
sam: is this the new canary that requests 2gpus-per-pod? we bumped it last week for perf testing
maria: correct, canary is 2 gpus. the bulk jobs are 1 gpu and are spread out, so we end up with 1-gpu islands
kevin: can confirm. saw evictions earlier where scheduler preempted 1-gpu jobs to try to consolidate but preemptions bounced back -> thrash :face_with_head_bandage:
infra-sre: logs from scheduler at 06:14 show lots of scoring churn: `nodeAffinityScore` oscillating, also taint-based evictions triggered by node.taint/gpu-scratch:NoSchedule in a few nodes
ops-bot: incident created INC-2026 (frag-sched-eu-west1), alerted on spike in Pending pods and increased preemptions
ryan: quick debug commands i ran: `kubectl get pods -n prod -o=custom-columns=NODE:.spec.nodeName,POD:.metadata.name,GPUS:.spec.containers[*].resources.requests` and `kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NODE:.metadata.name,ALLOC:.status.allocatable.nvidia.com/gpu,ALLOCATED:.status.allocatable` — shows usable GPUs but allocation mismatch
maria: also saw some nodes labelled `zone: eu-west1-b` with `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable=false` but they carry a `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` anti-affinity rule from a daemonset that forces spreading
sam: two-pronged mitigation idea: (1) temporarily relax canary 2-gpu requirement to 1 gpu so it schedules, or (2) run a targeted drain+pack on nodes with small leftover GPUs, consolidate 1-gpu jobs onto fewer nodes then free contiguous nodes for 2-gpu pods
kevin: both risky. (1) changes test footprint, might mask multi-gpu regressions. (2) causes disruption and will spike evictions/cold-starts for jobs. cost impact: consolidation will increase preemptions, short-term more API retries
infra-sre: we can do a less-disruptive pack using `descheduler` with the `RemoveDuplicates` and `LowNodeUtilization` strategies set to threshold 0.35 — that will move low-priority pods off nodes to decrease fragmentation without mass preemption
ryan: another lever: use the scheduler's `binpack` plugin you demoed — set policy `preferredNodeAffinity` to prefer nodes with >=2 free GPUs for the canary class. fallback to standard if not found. doesn't require killing jobs, just scoring preference
maria: do we have a quick way to find nodes with contiguous free GPUs? i tried a prometheus query: `sum by(node) (kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="nvidia.com/gpu"}) - sum by(node) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="nvidia.com/gpu"})` and it gives integers per node but doesn't reflect fragmentation inside node if multiple gpus are carved by MIG. we also have MIG annotation on nodes though
kevin: fragmentation also coming from mixed instance types — some nodes have 8xA100, others 4xA100, and our allocator doesn't respect GPU packing per-device. scheduler thinks there are 4 free GPUs when actually they are 4 separate MIG slices used by different tenants
sam: short-term plan: 1) disable canary 2-gpu requirement for next deploy (temporary flag) and run descheduler with low node utilization on a curated subset of nodes in eu-west1-b only; 2) open a task to add a binpack-aware extender that understands per-device allocation and MIG; 3) remind infra team to avoid creating many 1-gpu burst jobs at same time
maria: SGTM. where do we run the descheduler job? i can run it in prod targeting label `gpu-pool=shared-eu-west1-b`
ryan: run as a dry-run first with `--v=4` and `--policy-config-file=/etc/descheduler/policy-lowutil.yaml` then 30m window with real mode if it looks safe
ops-bot: @sam commented on INC-2026: "running descheduler dry-run now, will follow up with pack plan"
kevin: also add a temporary node annotation `scheduler.alpha.kubernetes.io/prefer-contiguous-gpus=true` for nodes we want as packing targets; scheduler scoring can weight that
infra-sre: action items: (a) sam to toggle canary gpu request flag (temp) — ETA 15m, (b) ryan to run descheduler dry-run on subset — ETA 20m, (c) maria to identify target nodes and tag them — ETA 10m, (d) kevin to open RFC for extender/MIG-aware packing — assigned
maria: doing annotations now, tagging 6 nodes: gw-eu-01..06 with `pack-target=true`
sam: toggled canary -> now requests 1 gpu for this run, triggering new canary deployment :eyes:
ryan: dry-run results: descheduler would evict 12 low-priority pods across 4 nodes, mostly test jobs older than 2h. no critical pods affected. looks safe to proceed
maria: proceeding to real-run descheduler on tagged nodes. will watch for crashloop spikes and API error metrics
kevin: keeping an eye on cost dashboard — if eviction churn increases, let me know so I can raise scale-down cooldowns
infra-sre: update: after descheduler run some nodes consolidated, 3 contiguous nodes now show 2+ free GPUs each and canary scheduled successfully on gw-eu-03
maria: canary passed health checks. rolling canary continues :tada:
sam: follow-ups: open INC-2026 update summarizing cause=fragmentation+MIG, mitigations=descheduler pack + temp canary downgrade, next-steps=RFC for MIG-aware scheduler extender. i'll file ticket
kevin: posted cost note to #finance about short-term bump from consolidation churn
ops-bot: INC-2026 updated: status=mitigated, notes=canary scheduled after packing, monitoring for recurrence
maria: thanks all. let's keep an eye on eu-west1 for next 6h and consider running periodic packing during low-traffic windows to avoid this repeating
ryan: +1, maybe a nightly defragment job at 0300 UTC with safety gates
kevin: if it becomes frequent we should consider reserving small 2-GPU pools for multi-gpu workloads rather than relying on on-the-fly packing
infra-sre: will add postmortem notes to the incident. closing thread once RFC is filed
maria: closing now — ping if anything pops back up :wave:
